translations.title: To the Name of Jesus
translations.text:
The cheerful flame of a warm hearth is sweet

to the traveler on a cold night;

the cool shade of a leafy grove is sweet

to one who walks beneath a burning sun.


The sound of a spring is sweet as sweetest music

to the thirsty; and breathing open air is sweet

to one who leaves an impious dungeon.


Rain is sweet, then, to the farmer;

warlike fame is sweet to the soldier;

and home soil is sweet to the pilgrim.


But more than air, shade, spring, flame,

rain, homeland, laurel, divine Jesus,

your name is sweet to the heart that loves you.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To the Sun on a December Day
translations.text:
Reign in the sky, O sun, reign and set

my weary breast alight with your life-giving fire!

Without light or vigor, cramped and hemmed in,

it longs for one ray of your burning flame.


At your blessed touch let the grass spring up;

let ice dissolve beneath your radiance.

Come forth despite the stubborn winter,

king of the sphere, O sun: my voice calls you!


From the happy fields where my cradle

received the treasure of your rays,

fate has driven me forever away.


Beneath another sky, in another land I weep,

where oppressive mist weighs upon me.

Break through it, sun; I implore you!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To Washington
translations.text:
In the past your virtue has no model;

history will offer no copy of it to the future;

nor will the passing centuries spread a memory

of any other equal to yours in greatness.


Europe saw the genius of war and victory

stain its soil with blood;

but to America fell the glory

of receiving from heaven the genius of good.


Let the bold conqueror revel in his skill

as he turns the world into a wasteland,

and boast of ruling slaves;


but peoples will know in their hearts

that only he who rules them free is strong,

and only he who makes them great is great!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To Fate
translations.text:
It was written, yes: in vain I break

the fatal chain again and again,

and strive to regain my strength.

It was written: heaven condemns me

to return always to harsh captivity,

and obediently I come,

restoring the links

that bind me tighter every time;

for the last convulsions of my pride

do not free me from the fated yoke.


Here I am! I am yours! Dispose, O fate,

of your docile victim! I surrender

like a dry leaf to the swift whirlwind

that blindly sweeps it away.

I am yours! Here I am! You can do anything!

Your whim is my law: sate your malice...

But know, O cruel one, that I am not deceived

by the false smile you grant me today.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To a Young Mother on the Loss of Her Child
translations.text:
Why do you weep, O Emilia, in such pain?

“Alas, I have lost the angel who was my delight...

Not even faint traces

of his lovely feet remain upon the earth.”


“You are mistaken, young mother; temper your grief.

That angel, though he flies free,

still follows you in love

wherever your wandering steps may lead.


Do you not marvel, when the gentle sphere

is bathed in the first light of rosy dawn,

at the harmony with which

heaven and earth greet the new day?


Then know, young mother, that each dawn

is colored by an angel's hands,

and his sweet voice

teaches that music to nature.


When the sun's last ray expires,

do you not hear a sigh circling around you?

And does a gentle breath

not caress your face and stir your curls?...
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Songs of Rejoicing and Victory...
translations.text:
Songs of rejoicing and victory

our voices raised on that day

when a royal mortal hand placed on you

the meager laurel of earthly glory.


And today, as you answer your Maker's call

to receive the shining diadem

that the unchanging Supreme Majesty

keeps for the virtuous in the eternal homeland,


our frail human nature strives in vain

to lift its breath to such heights.

It cannot draw, noble Quintana,

even a tender farewell from the grieving lyre!


For though Faith with divine radiance

lights the dense night of the tomb,

and Hope flies to the lofty summit,

showing the path of your triumph,


here, watching your mortal remains

return to earth, we have only,

with the crown Spain inherits from you,

grief in our hearts and tears in our eyes!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: This Evening, Christ of Calvary...
translations.text:
This evening, Christ of Calvary,

I came to pray to you for my ailing flesh;

but seeing you, my eyes move back and forth

from your body to mine in shame.


How can I complain of my tired feet

when I see yours torn apart?

How can I show you my empty hands

when yours are full of wounds?


How can I tell you of my loneliness

when you hang alone upon the cross?

How can I tell you I have no love

when your heart has been torn open?


Now I remember nothing at all;

all my ailments have fled from me.

The urgent prayer I brought

chokes in my pleading mouth¹.


And I ask only to ask nothing of you,

to be here beside your lifeless image,

learning that pain alone

is the holy key to your holy door.

Amen.




1. Pleading: asking frequently and insistently.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To the Castilian Banner
translations.text:
Hail, illustrious banner of Castile,

that waves today upon the walls of Tétouan

and sends to the Cuban Antilles

reflections of Spain's glories!

The crescent, which bows before you,

now recalls how, amid turbulent waves,

to the deep dread of Hagar's descendants,

it sank when Lepanto's star arose.


And those Moors, a disgrace to Europe,

who forgot the roar of your lions,

today, beneath the harsh blow that chastens them,

conjure fierce visions in their fear.

In the bloody light of seven centuries

they think they see, rising amid coats of arms,

with their turbans spread beneath their feet,

the shades of El Cid, Alfonso, and Guzmán.


Oh yes! Those august names go with you

and fight for you; the rays of their glory

flash in your folds, as they shine

throughout Spanish history.

May they forever triumph as symbols

of honor and victory, while civilization

proudly watches Tétouan welcome you today,

and Tangier tomorrow!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To ****
translations.text:
No bond remains: everything is broken.

Heaven willed it so: blessed be its will!

I gladly drain the bitter cup;

my soul rests at last and desires nothing.


I loved you; I love you no longer—or so I think.

If I am wrong, may I never see the truth!

Let oblivion swallow so many bitter years;

let my heart breathe again.


You shattered it without pity; my pride

you trampled over and over in your frenzy...

Yet my lips will never breathe a murmur

to accuse you of your tyranny.


As the dread avenger of grave offenses,

you dutifully fulfilled your mission; do you know it?

The irresistible power that laid my strength

prostrate before you was not yours.


God willed it, and so it was: glory to his name!

All is over; I draw breath again.

Angel of vengeance! You are a man now...

I feel neither love nor fear when I behold you.


Your scepter fell, your sword grew dull...

But ah, how sadly I breathe this freedom!

I made a world of you, and now it falls to nothing,

leaving me in deep and boundless solitude.


May you live happily! If someday

you see this farewell I send you forever,

know that in my soul you still have

generous forgiveness and tender affection.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
